recipe: Minimize component state by deriving values from existing state instead of storing them separately; for example, do not add an isEmpty state when you already have an items array.
trigger_condition: When deciding what data to store in component state during development.
evidence: If a component uses a value which can be derived from another piece of state, then that value should most likely not be part of the state.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Consolidate state within the top-level component and make subcomponents pure and stateless when a component has multiple subcomponents.
trigger_condition: When a component has multiple subcomponents that share or depend on the same data.
evidence: If a component has multiple subcomponents, it'll be best if it's possible to consolidate the state within the top level and the rest of the components are pure and stateless.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Disable interactive elements while they trigger an async request to prevent double-firing from accidental double clicking.
trigger_condition: When a component's interactive elements initiate an asynchronous network request.
evidence: Disable interactive elements if they trigger an async request! Prevents double firing of events in the case of accidental double clicking
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Debounce or throttle search input so that each keystroke does not fire a separate network request.
trigger_condition: When implementing a search input that triggers a network request.
evidence: If there are search inputs involved, each keystroke should not fire a network request.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Display an explicit empty state when a list has no items, rather than rendering nothing.
trigger_condition: When a component renders a list that may be empty.
evidence: Display an empty state if there are no items in a list, instead of not rendering anything.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Add a confirmation step before executing destructive or irreversible actions.
trigger_condition: When implementing a destructive or irreversible user action in a component.
evidence: Destructive actions should have a confirmation step, especially irreversible ones.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Reflect component state to the user by showing spinners for pending requests and displaying errors instead of failing silently.
trigger_condition: When a component performs async operations or can enter an error state.
evidence: Reflect state of the component to the user - If there's a pending background request, show a spinner. If there's an error, make sure to display it instead of silently failing.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Handle extreme input cases by truncating long strings behind a 'View more' button and paginating or constraining the display of large item lists.
trigger_condition: When a component can receive very long strings or a large number of items to display.
evidence: Strings can be really long/short and your UI should not look weird in either case. For long strings, they can have their contents truncated and hidden behind a "View more" button.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Make the component keyboard-friendly by adding shortcuts, ensuring all elements can be focused, and verifying correct tab order.
trigger_condition: When building an interactive UI component that must support keyboard-only users.
evidence: Ensure that elements can be focused and tab order within the component is correct
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Clarify requirements thoroughly before drawing any architecture, spending at least a few minutes asking clarifying questions about devices, browsers, i18n, and styling needs.
trigger_condition: When starting a front end system design interview for a UI component.
evidence: Do not start drawing the architecture before you are clear about the requirements!
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Use windowing/virtualization to render only the visible subset of a long list, preserving scroll height so the UI appears unoptimized to the user.
trigger_condition: A component must render hundreds or thousands of items (e.g. a selector or carousel) where only a few are visible at a time.
evidence: We can leverage a technique called windowing/virtualization to emulate a list with many elements while only rendering a few as possible to make the final result look as if there was no optimization done (especially preserving scroll height).
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Load only the items within the viewport or most likely to be viewed, and load the rest on demand rather than eagerly.
trigger_condition: A component contains a large collection of resources (e.g. hundreds of photos in a gallery) that cannot all be loaded at once.
evidence: An optimization could be to load only the ones that the user is likely to view, or those that are within the viewport (which we call "above the fold"). The rest of the photos can be loaded on demand
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Prefetch or preload the next item(s) the user is likely to request while they are still interacting with the current one, so the next action requires no network wait.
trigger_condition: A component has a predictable next step (e.g. an image carousel where the user will click Next).
evidence: an optimization could be to load the next image ahead of time while the user is still on the current image, such that when the user clicks the "Next" button, there's no network delay needed because the next image has already been loaded
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Ensure foreground colors have sufficient contrast against background colors to support users with color blindness.
trigger_condition: Designing or reviewing the visual styling of a UI component.
evidence: Foreground colors should have sufficient contrast from the background colors
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Use semantically correct HTML tags or appropriate aria-role attributes so screen readers and assistive technology can interpret the component structure.
trigger_condition: Building any interactive UI component that needs to be accessible to non-visual users.
evidence: Use the right HTML tags for semanticness, or the right `aria-role` attributes
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Add a tabindex attribute to make clickable items focusable via keyboard, and apply cursor: pointer styling to visually indicate interactivity.
trigger_condition: Creating any clickable or interactive element in a component.
evidence: Clickable items should have `tabindex` attribute (so that they are focusable) and also "cursor: pointer" styling to indicate that they can be clicked on
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Provide alt text for every image so screen readers can describe it and it serves as a fallback if the image fails to load.
trigger_condition: Including images in a component.
evidence: Images should have `alt` text, which will be read out by screen readers and act as a fallback description if the image fails to load
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Add an aria-label attribute to icon buttons or other elements that lack a visible text label so non-visual users understand their purpose.
trigger_condition: Using an icon button or any element whose function is non-obvious without a text label.
evidence: an icon button without any text label within it should have an `aria-label` attribute so that the intention is clear for users who can't see the icon
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Pass display strings as props with an English default instead of hardcoding them, so the component can be localized for other languages.
trigger_condition: A component uses display strings (e.g. button labels like "Prev"/"Next").
evidence: Strings used in the component shouldn't be hardcoded to a specific language (e.g. "Prev"/"Next" in the controls of a photo gallery component). The strings can be specified as a prop with the English version as default
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Verify that the component's layout supports right-to-left language rendering when the order of content matters.
trigger_condition: A component's layout depends on the order of content (e.g. text direction, icon placement).
evidence: Does your component support RTL (right to left) languages like Arabic and Hebrew?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Keep the amount of JavaScript bundled with a component minimal to reduce download size and network request time.
trigger_condition: Designing or refactoring a component's codebase for performance.
evidence: The less JavaScript the component contains, the less JavaScript the browser has to download to load the component and the lower the network request time.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Modularize components so users only download the JavaScript modules they actually need for their use case.
trigger_condition: Building a component library or feature set where different users need different subsets of functionality.
evidence: It's also important to modularize components and allow users to download only the necessary JavaScript modules needed for their use case.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Minimize the amount of JavaScript executed and DOM updates during user interactions so the UI can respond as quickly as possible.
trigger_condition: Handling any user interaction (click, input, scroll) in a component.
evidence: The less work (JavaScript executed, DOM updates) the component has to do when a user does something on the page, the faster the component can update the UI to respond to the changes.
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Avoid rendering user input via innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities.
trigger_condition: A component renders user-provided input into the DOM.
evidence: Do you render user input via `.innerHTML` or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (React-specific)?
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Increase the hit box size of interactive elements so users on touch devices can reliably tap the intended target.
trigger_condition: Designing a component for mobile web where users interact via fingers rather than a mouse.
evidence: Increasing the hit box of interactive elements - fingers have an easier time tapping on the right element
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)

recipe: Consciously limit memory usage in the component because excessive memory consumption makes mobile devices perform slower.
trigger_condition: Targeting mobile web where hardware is less powerful and viewport is smaller.
evidence: Not use too much memory - using too much memory makes the device perform slower
source_name: Front End Interview Handbook: Front end system design (UI components)
